Welcome to today's lecture on Linear Algebra, specifically the topic of Eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Let us consider a square matrix A. Of A if multiplying A by V only scales V, without changing its direction. The scaling factor is called the eigenvalue, usually denoted by the Greek letter lambda. So the defining equation is A times V equals lambda times V, To find eigenvalues, we rewrite the equation as a minus lambda times I. Times V equals zero.
